resolved_prior_findings.basis: The compiled rows (/tmp/morning-actual-aligned-rows.xml) show that every Bible key in morning_entrance_verses and morning_before_prayer pairs the morning Hebrew with the morning English in the same service context. None of them pairs with the s7 Hebrew. Clear evidence: the first Psalm 17:6 row (rows file lines 85 and 90) has the s40 Hebrew כִּי־תַעֲנֵנִי with a dagesh, not the s7 כִי־תַעֲנֵנִי (readings.json:67). So the documentary build uses the s40 witness and does not use a project-wide first-copy lookup. Round 2's parts (b) and (c) were inferred from the guideline. The compiled output shows they were wrong for documentary alignment. The guideline also supports the actual behaviour: lines 2102-2103 scope the dropped repeated corresp to 'within a document', and each morning file declares each key only once. Lines 302-307 say a second printing 'is not an error; but only the first copy can be reached by its URN'. That is the documented expanded-edition behaviour: unbound transclusions at expanded index.xml:1203-1223 resolve to the s7 witness and its pointing. The canonical_selection_note in /tmp/morning-alignment-verification.json and readings.json:10501 and :9943 record this decision. The guideline does not require choosing the later printing.

Both repeat module files are gone (Read on he/ and en/morning_psalm_17_6_repeat.xml reports 'File does not exist'), and nothing in the snapshot transcludes them. The second Psalm 17:6 is now written directly in the second paragraph of each before_prayer file (he:35, en:35) as follows: one occurrence milestone with corresp .../morning_preliminaries/psalm_17_6_repeat, then seg source=psalms/17/6, then a bare occurrence terminator, then chapter 26 opens. This puts the milestone before the semantic span, as guideline 212-215 requires. Each side has the occurrence URN exactly once. The compiled row (rows file lines 263 and 268) pairs the s42 Hebrew with 'I called to Thee for Thou dost respond to me. O God, …'. The seg/@source survives in the compiled output, so the loss of the source annotation noted in round 2 is gone. The first 17:6 is still Biblical (verse milestone, present tense 'I call to Thee, …'). Both English tenses are kept.

he/morning_mah_tovu.xml:33-39 now has the unique context div, an n39 facs div and an INLINE transclusion of prayer:mah_tovu@HE inside a p. The compiled row (rows file lines 51-67) is one paired row under the shared .../morning_preliminaries/mah_tovu context. The HE column has all five clauses: מַה־טֹּבוּ…יִשְׂרָאֵל: | וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב…בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ: | יְיָ אָהַבְתִּי…כְּבוֹדֶךָ: | וַאֲנִי אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה…עֹשִׂי: | וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי…יִשְׁעֶךָ:. They match both the s40 reading (readings.json:9818-9869) and the s7 reading (readings.json:56) letter for letter, so the 'identical paragraph' premise holds. The EN column has all five clauses with the mah_tovu/mah_tovu and varani part milestones and five seg/@source annotations, with 95:6 as type=adaptation. The row is not empty and no s7 text is placed out of position.

Information only, no change needed: (a) In the compiled HE Mah Tovu cell, inline transclusion strips the canonical's internal part milestones and segs, while the EN cell keeps them. verdict: approved. N1 is resolved: the compiled output shows that each morning Bible occurrence pairs in its own service context with the correct s40/s42 Hebrew and printed English, and the s7-first canonical choice for the expanded edition is documented and consistent with guideline 302-307. The F4 repeat module is removed and replaced by a direct occurrence encoding that keeps both English tenses and the Bible source annotation. The F2 Mah Tovu row is complete with all five clauses on both sides. All other round 2 approvals stand, there are no remaining source ambiguities, and I found no new transcription or encoding errors.
checks: First Psalm 17:6 compiled HE = s40 כִּי־ with dagesh (rows file line 85), against s7 כִי־ (readings.json:67). This shows the documentary build uses the morning witness and not the s7 one.
Second Psalm 17:6 compiled HE = s42 reading (readings.json:10283), EN = past tense (readings.json:10479); the occurrence URN appears once per side.
Mah Tovu s40 HE = s7 HE letter for letter (readings.json:9818-9869 vs :56), so reusing the canonical inline does not change the printed text.

Human confirmations (Shachar attribution, standard יְיָ, עֲטִיפַת without meteg, בַּתּוֹרָה, לְאַחְדּוּתוֹ dalet dagesh and vav shuruq) are reflected in readings.json:10531 and were not reopened. The round 2 image checks (סֵֽדֶר meteg; no maqaf in אֶל אַנְשֵׁי, readings.json:10583) remain settled.

Not independently verified: the runtime fields evening_yigdal_uses_new_witness=false for ordinary_shabbat and minchah. Those cases are marked passed, and I take false to be the expected value because those services contain no evening Yigdal, but the report does not say so. Also not verified: that the registry note siddur.jsonl:1995 is up to date (carried over from round 2; outside the files I was given).
